title: Task evals: grant Bash/Write/Edit and stage a sandbox-readable toolchain
description: The first claude plugin eval task run (2026-09-26, /tmp/test-skills-plugin-eval/20260926-164748) was invalid: plugin eval gates Bash/Write/Edit behind --allow-tools, so all 10 agents were read-only. Probes then showed that the eval OS sandbox cannot exec from /Volumes/external, cannot read home (the uv interpreter's stdlib lives there), and breaks the /usr/bin xcrun shims (git, python3). The sandbox is not configurable (plugin-evals docs), so the runner must stage a toolchain outside home and put it on PATH.

acceptanceCriteria.text: run_plugin_eval.sh passes --allow-tools Bash Write Edit for task cases
A toolchain outside home (relocatable CPython + pinned venv + direct git) is built and prepended to PATH
A sandbox probe confirms python+pytest, git commit, and npx vitest/stryker work inside an eval run
Runbook documents the sandbox constraints and the toolchain

finalSummary:
The first plugin-eval task run was invalid: all 10 agents were read-only because --allow-tools was not passed. The runner now passes --allow-tools Bash Write Edit for task cases.

Probes showed the eval OS sandbox cannot be configured. It does not exec from /tmp, /Volumes or the uv venv. Home is unreadable. The xcrun shims fail. evals/eval_toolchain.sh builds a relocatable CPython with the pinned deps at /tmp/test-skills-toolchain. Each task scaffold calls evals/stage_toolchain.sh, which clones it into the run's home (.tc) with wrappers for python, git and npm/npx, and puts them on PATH via .zshenv.

Sandbox probes confirmed the fix. The shop scaffold ran pytest, tmx collect-pytest (172 tests), git history and workspace writes. The TS fixture ran npx vitest 4.1.11 and npx stryker 10.0.0. The runbook documents all of this. Delivered in the PR that closes this task.
